### Findings

**1. Dead export in the new schema file — [`schemas/rhinestone-error.schema.ts:24-26`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/chore/improve-relay-service-logging/src/modules/relay/datasources/schemas/rhinestone-error.schema.ts#L24-L26)**

`RhinestoneErrorResponse` is exported but nothing imports it — `rhinestone-api.service.ts` imports only `RhinestoneErrorResponseSchema`. This is dead code (YAGNI).

```ts
export type RhinestoneErrorResponse = z.infer<
  typeof RhinestoneErrorResponseSchema
>;
```

Delete these three lines. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fmodules%2Frelay%2Fdatasources%2Fschemas%2Frhinestone-error.schema.ts%20on%20branch%20chore%2Fimprove-relay-service-logging%2C%20delete%20the%20unused%20exported%20type%20alias%20RhinestoneErrorResponse%20on%20lines%2024-26.%20Nothing%20imports%20it.&repo=safe-global/safe-client-gateway)

**2. Literal fixtures in three of the new tests — [`rhinestone-api.service.spec.ts:214`, `:247`, `:268`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/chore/improve-relay-service-logging/src/modules/relay/datasources/rhinestone-api.service.spec.ts#L214)**

The three "should not log the context…", "should collapse newlines…" and "should cap the number of…" tests hard-code `{ status: 400, statusText: 'Bad Request' }`. The pre-existing sibling test and the first new case both use `faker.internet.httpStatusCode(...)` + `faker.lorem.words()`, which is what the testing guide requires (builders + faker; no literal fixtures — R-004).

Replace with the same pattern already used in the file:

```ts
const status = faker.internet.httpStatusCode({ types: ['clientError'] });
const statusText = faker.lorem.words();
// … { status, statusText } as Response …
// expected log line: `status=${status} ${statusText} …`
```

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fmodules%2Frelay%2Fdatasources%2Frhinestone-api.service.spec.ts%20on%20branch%20chore%2Fimprove-relay-service-logging%2C%20replace%20the%20hard-coded%20%7B%20status%3A%20400%2C%20statusText%3A%20%27Bad%20Request%27%20%7D%20literals%20at%20lines%20214%2C%20247%20and%20268%20with%20faker%20values%20-%20const%20status%20%3D%20faker.internet.httpStatusCode(%7B%20types%3A%20%5B%27clientError%27%5D%20%7D)%3B%20const%20statusText%20%3D%20faker.lorem.words()%3B%20-%20and%20interpolate%20them%20into%20the%20expected%20log%20line%2C%20matching%20the%20pattern%20already%20used%20in%20the%20preceding%20tests%20in%20the%20file.&repo=safe-global/safe-client-gateway)

**3. Nit — `.slice()` before `.filter()` in `describeUpstreamError` — [`rhinestone-api.service.ts:116-119`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-client-gateway/blob/chore/improve-relay-service-logging/src/modules/relay/datasources/rhinestone-api.service.ts#L116-L119)**

```ts
const messages = (parsed.data.errors ?? [])
  .slice(0, MAX_LOGGED_UPSTREAM_ERRORS)
  .map((error) => this.truncateForLog(error.message))
  .filter((message) => message.length > 0);
```

If the first N entries have whitespace-only messages, all diagnostic content is dropped even when later entries would carry a real reason. Filtering *before* slicing would preserve the diagnosis. Very minor — Rhinestone is unlikely to emit empty leading messages — feel free to keep as-is.

### Otherwise
- Log-injection guard (`\s+` collapse), length cap, and the deliberate `context` omission are correctly modelled by the schema (undeclared keys stripped) and asserted by the "should not log the context" test — nicely done.
- The "keep the provider error detail out of the thrown error" test is a good regression guard against future leaks of upstream text into the client-facing payload.
- `formatError` is shared correctly with `getTaskStatus`; the `NetworkRequestError` branch also has a test.
